items.text: Where can I see what's happening with my transfer?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

You can check your transfer status by logging into your Wise account, going to Home to see your activity list, and clicking on the specific transfer you want to track. From there, you'll see statuses like "Your money's being processed," "Money received," or "Transfer Sent."

items.text: What do the different stages in the tracker mean?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

The tracker shows three main stages: "Your money's being processed" means we're waiting for your bank to send funds. "Money received" means we have your cash and are converting it. Finally, "Transfer Sent" means we've sent the money to your recipient's bank, but their bank may take a few working days to deliver it.

Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: My payment has said processing since Tuesday, is that normal?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

If your transfer has been on "Your money's being processed" for more than two working days, you should check with your bank to ensure they've sent the funds to us. Weekends and public holidays also delay processing as banks don't work then.

items.text: What does transfer sent mean?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

When your transfer status shows "Transfer Sent," we have sent the money to your recipient's bank. From there, their bank will process and deliver it, which can take a few working days depending on the currency. Your money is safely on its way, but the tracker might not update again until it arrives in their account. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: How long until the money shows up for my recipient?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

We give an estimated delivery time when you set up your transfer, but delays can happen at any stage. Your money is on its way to the recipient bank, and they might take up to one working day to release it. If it's taking longer than expected, ask them to check their bank statement for a transaction from Wise or our banking partners using the reference number you received.

items.text: It was supposed to arrive today and nothing's there.

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

We mark transfers as complete once we've sent the money to your recipient's bank, but their bank may take up to one working day to release it. Your recipient can check their bank statement for a transaction from Wise or use a transfer receipt to help locate the payment. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: Do bank holidays slow transfers down?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

Yes, bank holidays can slow transfers down because banks don't process payments on weekends or public holidays. Our delivery estimates only count working days, so if you send money before a holiday, it might not move until the next working day. This applies to both the country you're sending from and the one you're sending to.

items.text: Will a small typo in the name stop the payment?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

Small typos in names usually don't stop payments, but for some currencies like JPY, they can be an issue. If there's a mistake in account details, your money might take longer or get returned to us. We'll let you know immediately if that happens. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: The person I paid says they haven't received a thing.

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

We mark your transfer as complete once we've sent the money to their bank, but their bank may take up to one working day to release it. They should check their statement for Wise or look for a transaction from our banking partners using the reference number you received. If they still can't find it, they might need to ask their bank to speed up the process with a transfer receipt. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: How do I get a receipt to send to my recipient's bank?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

To get a receipt, log into your Wise account, click on your transfer, and use the Get PDF receipt button in your browser or app. Save it to your device and send it to your recipient so their bank can track the money. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: Why is it marked completed if my brother still can't see the money?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

We mark your transfer as complete once we've sent the money to your brother's bank. His bank might still be processing it, which can take up to one working day. He should check his bank statement for a transaction from Wise or our banking partners using the reference number you provided.

items.text: What name will show on my recipient's bank statement?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

Your recipient won't see your name on their bank statement. Instead, they might see the sender as Wise or one of our banking partners. They can identify the transfer using the reference number provided to them. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: The amount that arrived is different from what I sent.

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

If the amount differs, your recipient's bank may have converted the currency again, resulting in a different total. You can check the transfer receipt for details on the currencies involved. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: Why is this taking so long?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

Delays can happen if your bank hasn't sent the money yet, there are security checks, or it's a weekend or holiday. Your recipient's bank might also be slow to process it once we've sent it. Check your tracker for the current status and ask them to share a transfer receipt with their bank if needed. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: How long does a bank transfer take to reach Wise?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

Bank transfers usually take one to four working days to reach us. Delays can happen due to weekends, holidays, security checks, or mistakes in your details. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: Is paying by card faster than a bank transfer?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

Yes, card payments are usually instant, while bank transfers can take one to four working days to reach us.

items.text: Why would you need to verify my information?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

Sometimes we need extra information to meet regulations. If we do, we'll send you an email explaining what we need. Keep an eye on your inbox so you can provide it quickly. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: My transfer is coming back to me, why?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

If your transfer is returning to you, it's likely because there was a mistake in the recipient's details, such as a typo in their name or account number. Their bank may have rejected the payment and sent it back. You can check your activity list to confirm this status.

items.text: What counts as a proof of payment?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

A proof of payment is a document showing you've sent money from your bank account. It could be a PDF of your bank statement, a screenshot from your online bank, or other file types less than 10MB and up to five files per altogether. To accept it, the document must clearly show your details, your bank's name or logo, our details, the date, amount, currency, and reference. We can't accept text copied and pasted into an email, a photo of your computer screen, bank-card photos, Wise receipts, nor password-protected files. For Swift payments, we need a pacs.008 document. For payments from Australia or New Zealand, we also need a recent bank statement showing your name, the date of issue, and your bank details. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: Can I upload two screenshots as proof?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

Yes, you can send us two screenshots if one doesn't show all the required details. Both must clearly display your bank account number to confirm they are from the same account. We cannot accept text copied and pasted or photos of computer screens. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: What file size can my bank statement be?
What does a pacs.008 document mean for Swift payments?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

For Swift payments, the proof of payment we need is a PACS.008 document. This is required when we ask for verification to ensure your money came from an account in your name. We can't accept text copied and pasted or photos of computer screens; please upload a high-quality screenshot or PDF instead. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: Where does my recipient use the reference number?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER
Your recipient uses the banking partner reference number to see where the transfer is once it shows as complete on your Wise account. They can give this number to their bank if they need to check on the payment, as banks might call it a UTR or transaction reference number depending on the country.

items.text: What's the difference between the transfer number and the partner reference?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

For every transfer you send with Wise, we give you a transfer number to use if you need to get in touch with us. For some transfers, we also give you a banking partner reference number because we send your money through local partners. You should give the partner reference number to your recipient so they can see where the transfer is once it shows as complete on your Wise account. They will need to give this number to their bank if they get in touch with them, as banks might call it something else like a UTR number.
